summary: Retry after OAuth refresh. Reconciled this worktree's pre-existing origin-thread/outbox groundwork in AITools/taskdb.py + AITools/taskctl.py against the two retained sibling worktrees (17fbfa4e0396... second B376 candidate, and 2a9878e97b90... an earlier fuller B343 DeepSeek/live-output candidate). Discovered and fixed a broken import chain (dashboard.py/process_launcher.py imported a nonexistent geoai_task_mcp.deepseek_credentials module in THIS worktree, and runtime_adapters.py lacked the DeepSeek constants/app-server command builder both callers already referenced) that would have failed collection on every listed test file. Implemented the missing callback_bridge.py App Server client from scratch against the real installed Codex 0.144.1 wire protocol (verified byte-for-byte via the coordinator-supplied SHA256 hashes of ClientRequest.json/ServerNotification.json found at /tmp/geoai-codex-app-server-schema/): no top-level jsonrpc member, initialize.params.clientInfo required, thread/resume.params.threadId required, turn/start.params.{threadId,input[]} required with optional cwd/clientUserMessageId, turn/completed arrives as an un-ided notification correlated by threadId. Added a real fake-executable App Server subprocess test harness and a proper assert-based pytest suite (the two retained candidates' test_callback_bridge.py used a print/counter PASS-FAIL pattern that pytest would silently report all-green regardless of internal failures -- replaced with real asserts). Implemented the two 'Focused review repair' items: episode-scoped outbox dedup (UNIQUE now includes episode_id, sourced from a new card claim_epoch counter bumped on every successful claim-start) with a fail-closed idempotent table-rebuild migration for pre-existing 3-column-UNIQUE databases, and an atomic pre-delivery supersede check in claim_pending_callback (a pending/inflight entry whose task is no longer in the matching review/blocked terminal state is marked superseded and never handed to the bridge). Fixed the legacy/default recover-stale path to route to blocked+terminal_outcome+outbox wake instead of silently requeuing to pending, and extended reject-review to also reclaim a blocked task (not only review), since blocked tasks had no other path back to pending. Updated the two now-stale exact-claim tests whose assertions predated the coordinator-review-first release-launch semantics.

read_first_reconciliation.earlier_b343_candidate_2a9878e9: /tmp/geoai-task-mcp-worktrees/2a9878e97b904d5aa8102b03465c6337/worktree -- has a working deepseek_credentials.py + the matching runtime_adapters.py DeepSeek constants/argv branch (DEEPSEEK_COPILOT_ADAPTER, resolve_deepseek_model, DEEPSEEK_SECRET_ENV_VAR) that THIS worktree's process_launcher.py already imports but runtime_adapters.py never defined. Ported byte-compatible: copied deepseek_credentials.py verbatim, merged the DeepSeek constants/argv branch into this worktree's runtime_adapters.py alongside its own (this worktree's) build_codex_app_server_command/validate_app_server_command additions -- neither candidate had both pieces at once.
read_first_reconciliation.outcome: No blind overwrite: every reconciled file was diffed against both siblings first; only the specific missing/incompatible symbols were merged, never a whole-file replace.

findings_applied: JSONRPCRequest/JSONRPCNotification/JSONRPCResponse/JSONRPCError each require only id/method/params or id/result or id/error -- NO 'jsonrpc' field in the schema at all; callback_bridge.py never sends one.
InitializeParams requires only clientInfo (name+version); capabilities optional -- no protocolVersion field in the schema, so it is omitted from the built request.
ThreadResumeParams requires threadId; cwd is optional.
TurnStartParams requires threadId+input (input is an ARRAY of UserInput, e.g. [{type:'text', text:...}], not a bare object); cwd and clientUserMessageId are optional.
ClientNotification 'initialized' requires only 'method' -- no params key at all for that variant; callback_bridge.py sends {"method": "initialized"} with no params.
turn/completed is a ServerNotification (method+params{threadId,turn}, no request id) -- correlated by threadId, not by the original turn/start request id.

reconciled_from_sibling_worktrees: tools/geoai-task-mcp/src/geoai_task_mcp/deepseek_credentials.py (copied from the 2a9878e9 sibling verbatim; self-contained, compatible with this worktree's runtime_adapters.py after the merge below)

callback_bridge_py: AppServerClient: initialize/send_initialized/thread_resume/turn_start, no jsonrpc member, cwd on turn_start defaults to /home/shrek/GeoAI, deterministic_client_user_message_id() (sha256-derived, stable per task+transition+thread+episode -- a bridge restart mid-delivery reissues the identical id).
BusyThreadError subclass of AppServerError raised on a 'busy' thread/resume error -- deferral path never starts a parallel turn.

CallbackBridge wraps AITools/taskdb.py's outbox primitives directly (claim_pending_callback/mark_callback_delivered/mark_callback_dead_letter/requeue_callback/callback_outbox_stats) so the bridge and taskctl never disagree about outbox state; run_once/daemon/status/dry_run CLI commands.

build_app_server_command/AppServerClient executable accepts either a single binary string or an argv-prefix list ([sys.executable, path]) so tests can spawn the fake server without relying on the executable bit (chmod is denied in this sandbox).
fake_app_server_py: Real subprocess (spawned via Popen, never a mocked subprocess.run returncode). Enforces initialize->initialized->thread/resume->turn/start sequence; rejects out-of-order/missing steps with a JSON-RPC-shaped error. --busy and --crash-after flags for the deferral/crash-recovery tests.
taskdb_py_episode_and_supersede: callback_outbox gains episode_id column; UNIQUE constraint is now (task_id, transition, origin_thread_id, episode_id) instead of a task-lifetime-scoped 3-column key.

_migrate_callback_outbox_add_episode_column(): idempotent, fail-closed (BEGIN IMMEDIATE + rollback-on-exception) table rebuild for a pre-existing 3-column-UNIQUE table; preserves all rows at episode_id='0'.
current_claim_episode(conn, task_id) reads card.claim_epoch (new in taskctl.py, see below); enqueue_callback/maybe_enqueue_callback resolve and store it.

claim_pending_callback() now loops: reclaims expired leases, then for each candidate pending row checks _task_still_in_matching_terminal_state() (transition=='blocked' requires current canonical_status=='blocked'; every other eligible transition requires 'review', matching cmd_release_launch's own target_status mapping) -- a stale row is atomically marked 'superseded' (new 5th outbox state) and the loop continues to the next row, so a superseded entry is never handed to the bridge and never launches Codex.
taskctl_py: _atomic_claim_task(): every successful claim increments card.claim_epoch (starts unset/0, becomes 1 on first claim) -- this is the episode boundary the outbox dedup keys off.

cmd_reject_review(): now accepts status in {review, blocked} (previously review-only) and clears terminal_outcome on reclaim, so a blocked task (e.g. the B383 promotion_conflict case) is not stranded forever -- pending remains reachable ONLY through this explicit Codex decision.

cmd_recover_stale() legacy/default path (no --owner-confirm): now routes to status=blocked with terminal_outcome=blocked and an outbox wake (via maybe_enqueue_callback) instead of silently requeuing straight to pending -- coordinator-review-first, matching cmd_release_launch's own pattern. The --owner-confirm TTL-gated path is unchanged (out of this task's explicit scope: 'the legacy/default recover-stale path').
broken_import_chain_fixed: dashboard.py imported geoai_task_mcp.deepseek_credentials, which did not exist anywhere in this worktree (confirmed also missing in the retained 17fbfa4e sibling -- a pre-existing cross-candidate bug, not something either B376 attempt introduced). process_launcher.py imports the same module for CredentialError/load_credential. Both are now satisfied by the ported deepseek_credentials.py.

tests.failure_classification: ALL 35 failed/error cases are the documented outer-sandbox limitation: PermissionError on os.chmod/os.fchmod of a freshly-created 0600 token/log file, or 'git init' failing with 'chmod on .git/config.lock failed: Operation not permitted'. Verified by grepping the full failure log: 0 of the 35 failure blocks lack a PermissionError/chmod/'Operation not permitted' string. These are host-only security tests genuinely blocked by this worker sandbox's seccomp denial of chmod/fchmod/git-init (matches AGENTS.md/this task's own acceptance note); none are logic regressions from this change. Per-file breakdown: test_taskctl_exact_claim_start_mcp.py 11/13 blocked (chmod on coordinator.token in _make_env, present before this task and unrelated to this diff), test_runtime_adapters.py 6/? blocked (chmod on a synthetic 'claude'/'codex' fixture executable), test_process_launcher.py 9 blocked (os.fchmod on a process log file, process_launcher.py:429), test_process_launcher_security.py 5 blocked at fixture setup ('git init -q' inside the sandbox), test_server_runtime_wiring.py 2 blocked (chmod on coordinator.token).
